Short jacket with a gathered or ribbed waist and cuffs in a flight or bomber pattern other than the MA-1 (A-2, B-15, CWU-45/P, G-1).
Hooded pullover jacket of windproof or waterproof fabric with a part-length front opening.
Hooded insulated coat with a smooth outer shell, ending below the hip, cut for cold weather; a quilted one is the puffer coat.
Hip-length military-style cotton jacket with four front pockets in a pattern other than the M-65 (M-43, M-51, safari-style).
Square of cloth folded and worn in the breast pocket of a jacket.
Clear visor on a headband or hard-hat mount that protects the whole face from impact or splash.
Plugs worn in the ear canal to reduce noise reaching the ears.
Close-fitting head covering that also covers the neck and part or all of the face.
Band of fabric or knit worn round the head or ears, held by its own elastic or ties.
Elastic garment without boning worn under clothing to smooth or shape the figure; a boned shaping garment is the corset.
Sleeveless top held by shoulder straps or narrow shoulders, of jersey or light fabric.
Woven top cut for women, with a placket, tie, yoke or collar detail but not a full collared button front; that is the button-up shirt.
Trousers with a fly and waistband sold apart from a suit, tailored or casual, in any leg shape (wide-leg, straight, pleated).
Close-fitting stretch trousers without feet; footed versions are tights.
Wide-legged trousers cut to hang like a skirt, ending between knee and ankle.
Sleeveless knitted top, pullover or buttoned.
Cut-resistant leg aprons strapped over ordinary trousers for chainsaw work; they come in different hazard ratings.
Close-cut punk trousers with straps joining the legs, zips and D-rings, often with a detachable bum flap; usually tartan or black cotton.

also_called: thawb · ثوب · kandura · dishdasha · jalabiya · djellaba · gandoura
description: Loose ankle-length robe with long sleeves, pulled over the head, worn mostly by men in Arab, North African and Sudanese dress; includes the kandura, dishdasha, jalabiya, djellaba and gandoura.
Very wide flowing robe worn over a tunic and trousers in men's sets, or alone as a gown, in West African dress; the agbada is a variant.

also_called: tunic suit · kurta pyjama · ao dai · baju kurung · puletasi · شلوار قمیض

description: Long-sleeved robe whose fronts overlap and are held by a sash, belt or side fastenings (Mongolian deel, Bhutanese gho, Central Asian chapan); the kimono and yukata are listed separately.
Loose long-sleeved over-garment reaching the knee or ankle, worn by women over other clothes for modest dress in public, open-front or closed; the Iranian manteau is a variant.
Fitted knee-length coat with a standing collar, buttoned down the front, worn over close trousers such as churidar for weddings and formal South Asian dress; includes the achkan.

also_called: hijab · instant hijab · underscarf · tudung · حجاب

description: Pullover top of woven or stretch fabric with a V or crew neck, short sleeves and patch pockets, worn as a medical or care uniform; scrub trousers are work trousers.
Knee-length or longer button-front work coat of white or coloured cotton or polyester, worn over clothing in laboratories, clinics and workshops; some resist splashes or chemicals.
Coat made of fur pelts or faux fur worn pile-out (mink, fox, sable or faux fur); fur-trimmed or fur-lined coats and suede-out sheepskin coats are listed by their cut.
Matching top and bottom (trousers, shorts or skirt) in the same fabric or print, sold together as one outfit; a tailored jacket set is the business suit.
Sleeved jacket ending at the hip or above, fastened at the front, in a cut no other jacket here covers (blouson, cropped jacket, leather or suede jacket not for riding).
Pullover top in a team's colours and badges, of jersey or mesh, sold as a team, replica, retro or fan shirt; a cycling jersey is in Sports, Fitness & Recreation.
Protective coat-and-trousers set or one-piece suit with flame-, heat- and water-resistant layers worn by firefighters, aluminised proximity suits included; it comes in different hazard ratings.
Pair of straps worn over the shoulders and clipped or buttoned to the trousers to hold them up; stocking suspenders (garters) are hosiery accessories, not this kind.
Machine that rolls clay into even slabs.
Machine that mixes clay and removes air from it.
Kiln made for firing clay. Fuel, loading style and chamber size vary by model.
Wax sold for making candles.
Scissors made for craft cutting.
Electronic cutter that cuts paper, vinyl and fabric from a design on screen.
Press that applies heat and pressure to transfer designs onto fabric and other blanks.
Liquid glue made for crafts.
Paint made for decorating craft objects, chosen by the surface it goes on.
Compressor made to drive an airbrush.

also_called: soft pastel · oil pastel · hard pastel

description: Pen, fineliner or marker sold mainly for drawing, comics or painting.
Brush made for painting pictures; the hair and shape vary by model.
Stand that holds a canvas or board while it is painted.
Kit with a numbered printed outline, matching numbered paints and a brush, sold as one set.
Kit with a coded adhesive canvas, resin drills and an applicator, sold as one set.
Dye made for colouring fabric and fibre.
Long-bladed shears made for cutting fabric.
Frame or machine made for weaving cloth; hand and powered looms are both here.

also_called: cross-stitch kit · embroidery kit · needlepoint kit
description: Kit with printed or counted cloth, floss and needle for one design, sold as one set.
Gemstone bead drilled ready for stringing.
Pearl drilled ready for stringing.
Faceted glass or synthetic stone made to set or glue on.
Unsorted assortment of shells sold for crafts.
Torch or kit made for soldering, brazing or annealing jewellery.
Empty album made for scrapbooking.
Decorative rubber, clear or wooden stamp made for paper craft.
Ink pad made for decorative stamps.
Decorative paper masking tape.
Square paper sheets made for paper folding.

also_called: knitting kit · crochet kit · amigurumi kit · needle-felting kit
description: Kit with yarn or fibre, needles or hook and a pattern for one project, sold as one set.
Home console with its games built in, so you cannot load others; includes plug-and-play minis.
Handheld on which games are loaded, not built in. A handheld gaming PC counts here.
Console that works both docked to a TV and as a handheld.
Handheld with its one game built in on an LCD screen.
Headset that encloses the eyes and has its own computer and battery.
Headset that encloses the eyes and needs a console or PC to run it.
Coin-operated video arcade cabinet that stands upright and is played standing.
Smaller upright coin-operated video cabinet.
Coin-operated video cabinet built as a table, played seated across or beside it.
Coin-operated video cabinet with a seat for the player.
Enclosed or motion cabinet built around the player.
Small cabinet made to stand on a counter or bar.
Arcade-style controller with a joystick lever and buttons.
Arcade-style controller with all-button directional input and no lever.
Game on a cassette, floppy or disk-system card.
Physical card that holds only a key to download a game, not the game itself.
Full game downloaded from a console or PC store, held with no disc or cartridge.
Downloadable maps, levels, characters, artbook or wallpaper content for a game.
Rechargeable battery pack made for one game machine or controller.
Stand or dock that only charges the machine or controller.
Cable or adapter with a connector made for one console.
Memory card, drive or expansion in a format made only for one console.
Stand or mount made to hold one game machine.
Cartridge or unit that alters a game (Game Genie type).
Portal or reader that reads Toys-to-Life figures for a game.
Unit that plugs into a console to add processor, graphics or memory hardware so it runs games made for the upgraded system (32X type).
Adapter that adds a dial-up modem, broadband or wireless network connection to one console through its own port or bay. A standard USB network adapter is in Computers & Components.
Microphone made and sold to plug into a console as game input, for singing or voice commands. A headset is in Audio & Video; a speech microphone sold for computers is in Computers & Components.
Mouse or trackball made to plug into one console as pointing input. A mouse with a standard connector sold for computers is in Computers & Components.
Keyboard made to plug into one console for typing, programming or text entry in games. A keyboard with a standard connector is in Computers & Components.
Headset that encloses the eyes and holds a phone as its screen and computer.

also_called: Rumble Pak · Jump Pack · Vibration Pack

description: Circuit board, with its game ROMs or cartridge or disc slot, that runs games inside a coin-operated video cabinet (JAMMA, Naomi, Atomiswave, MVS type).
Dongle, adapter or board that translates a controller's signals so it works on a console or computer it was not made for. A plain cable is a console cable or adapter.
Force-feedback motor base sold without a rim; interchangeable rims mount on it by quick release. Drive type (direct, belt, gear) varies.
Game machine with its game built in and its own screen (VFD, LCD or LED), made to stand on a table, not held and not linked to a TV.
External fan, cooling stand or clip-on unit made to cool one console. A replacement internal fan is a replacement part.
Lever unit sold apart from a stick or yoke that sets engine power, often with flap or trim levers, in flight games and simulators. A stick-and-throttle set (HOTAS) is a flight stick.
Frame, stand or seat rig made to hold a racing wheel, pedals, shifter or flight controls for play. A gaming chair without controller mounts is in Furniture & Storage.
Headphones with an attached microphone, whatever they are used for.
In-ear earphones with shells moulded to one listener's ear, sold for listening.
Two separate wireless buds sold with a charging case.
Television whose picture is projected onto the screen from inside its cabinet.
Projector made to sit at the wall just below the image it throws.

also_called: single-enclosure speaker · Bluetooth speaker · party speaker
description: Self-contained speaker in one box that is neither a bar nor a bass-only speaker; wireless streaming, battery and multi-room are features, not separate types.
Speakers without a cabinet, with a mounting flange, built into a wall or ceiling.
Slim speaker cabinets made to hang flat on a wall, often beside a TV; in-wall speakers have no cabinet.

also_called: Bluetooth audio transmitter · Bluetooth audio receiver
sound processor · graphic equaliser · parametric equaliser
description: Stereo component for shaping the tone or sound field of a signal, such as a graphic or parametric equaliser or a digital sound processor; a surround decoder is an AV processor.
Home component that plays (and may record) 8-track tape cartridges; an 8-track player fitted in a car is in Vehicles.

also_called: Blu-ray player · DVD player · DVD recorder
terrestrial receiver · satellite receiver · cable box

description: Portable device sold mainly to play stored or streamed music, with no calling; a Toniebox-type player for children is listed here.
Figure that plays its stored content when placed on its player.

also_called: mini system · midi system · music centre

description: Portable radio-cassette or CD system with built-in speakers and a carry handle.
Machine that plays a selected record or track, however it is paid for, unless it is sold as an arcade or coin-operated game.
Remote made for one TV or audio system; a universal remote is listed here too.
Stand made to hold one speaker model.
Bracket, arm, wall mount or table stand made to hold one TV or speaker.
Painting in ground mineral pigments fixed with animal glue, on paper or silk, in the Japanese tradition.
A small painted portrait made as a work of its own, often on vellum, ivory, card or metal.
An image hand-painted in acrylic on a clear acetate sheet, made for an animated film.
An image sprayed onto paper, canvas or another sheet by a print head with pigment or dye inks.
An ornamental figure cast in pewter, zinc, tin or another non-bronze metal.
Script characters carved into a seal of stone or another material as a work of art, sold as the seal or its impressions.
A base, plinth or stand made for one sculpture.
An image made by pressing damp paper into a carved or built-up plate so the design stands in relief, mainly without ink. Embossing added to an inked print is not this.
Legal-tender coin struck for everyday circulation; a worn coin sold for its silver content (junk silver) is still this kind.
Set of coins issued and sold by a mint as one packaged product.
Note-like piece made as a film prop, demonstration note or souvenir and not legal tender.
Paper or other money issued to circulate as money by an issuer that is not a currency authority.
Cover carrying stamps cancelled on their day of issue, issued by a postal administration or prepared for the purpose.
Disc medal given for achievement in sport, school, military or other competition, finisher's medals included.
Belt awarded to a champion.
Ring awarded to the members of a championship team or to a champion.
Card inserted at a lower rate than the base set, including signed and relic cards.
Card printed on the box, panel or packaging of another product and cut from it.
Sticker from a numbered series, like Panini's, made to be collected into an album.
Unopened pack, box, blaster, hanger or case of cards.
Crown that is regalia of an office.
Land under trees, whether managed for timber, amenity or conservation.
A whole house standing free of neighbours. A factory-built home on a permanent foundation is also placed here.
A holding with no single main use: no one use covers more than half the area, or several uses are combined and none is sold as the main one. Area and enterprises are noted.
A small timber or tin-clad hut on wheels, made to stand in a garden or field as a room. One with its own sink, toilet and entrance is a tiny house on wheels.
A bay or space for parking a vehicle, owned as land (freehold or long lease). A rented bay or permit is not included.
Land laid out as a golf course, with or without a clubhouse.
Land laid out as a runway or landing strip for light aircraft, with or without hangars.

also_called: standard four-wheel tractor · compact tractor · sub-compact tractor
description: General-purpose wheeled tractor with a rear power take-off and a three-point hitch, made to pull, carry and drive implements. Makers label sizes sub-compact, compact or utility.

also_called: narrow tractor · tracteur fruitier · tracteur vigneron · Schmalspurtraktor

description: Wheeled tractor built and guarded for forest work such as winching and skidding; also shown under Forestry.
Self-propelled carrier made to carry and drive implements, with no load body. A Unimog with a load bed is in Vehicles.

also_called: tractor snow blade · tractor snow blower
description: Snow blade or blower mounted on or driven from a tractor.
Implement that sows seed in rows at a set rate and depth; the coulters may be tine, disc or no-till.
Machine that plants rice seedlings into a flooded paddy; usually four to eight rows.
Sprayer that applies crop-protection liquids through a boom; it may be mounted, trailed or self-propelled.
Hose reel and field sprinkler line made for irrigating field crops.
Self-moving span of sprinkler pipe that irrigates a field in a circle or a strip.
Pump made to move water for field irrigation.
Self-propelled machine that reaps, threshes and cleans grain; threshing may be head-feeding, conventional or axial rotor.
Machine that cuts and chops forage crops for silage; it may be self-propelled or trailed.
Implement that cuts and shreds standing vegetation on grassland, verges, vineyards and scrub.
Fixed parlour in which cows stand in stalls to be milked; one unit may serve two stalls or each stall, and stalls may sit abreast or in herringbone.
Handheld reader for livestock electronic ear tags, sold for herd recording; pet microchip scanners are in Animal Equipment.
Commercial hatcher for eggs at flock scale; small incubators are in Animal Equipment.
Machine that fells trees and gathers them into bunches; it may drive to each tree or swing a boom.
Chipper that is tractor-driven (PTO or mounted) or part of a forest machine; a towed or self-propelled tree-surgery chipper is in Garden & Grounds.
Excavator-based machine built for forestry work.
Log splitter driven from or mounted on a tractor; hand and engine log splitters are in Tools & Workshop Equipment.
Guidance receiver, display or auto-steer kit made for a tractor or farm machine.
Hydraulic loading crane made to be fitted to a forwarder, harvester or timber trailer.
Smartphone in one piece with a fixed physical keyboard below the screen.
Basic mobile phone in one rigid body with a keypad and no smartphone features; taco and other one-piece shapes included.
Mobile phone whose screen half slides over the keypad half.
Mobile phone whose screen half rotates on a pivot to show the keypad.

also_called: corded phone · cordless phone · DECT phone
description: Telephone for a fixed line, corded or cordless (DECT).
Two-way radio made to be installed in a vehicle.
Fixed two-way radio run from mains power at one site.
Touchscreen computer in one flat body, sold without a keyboard; an optional keyboard cover is sold separately.
Device sold for reading e-books, usually on an e-paper screen.
E-paper device sold for taking notes and handwriting with a stylus.
Pair of earbuds sold for translating speech between languages through a phone app; ordinary earbuds with a translate feature are in Audio & Video.
Wrist device with a display that runs apps and notifications; GPS sports watches are included.

also_called: smart band · fitness tracker · activity tracker

description: Glasses with a see-through display, camera or speakers; a headset that encloses the eyes is in Video Games.
Handheld GPS unit with a two-way radio in the same case.
Portable navigation unit with road maps, sold to be moved between vehicles; a mounted one is in Vehicles.
Tracker with its own GPS and cellular link (SIM, subscription), carried by a person or put in a bag; animal trackers are in Animal Equipment, vehicle trackers in Vehicles.
Portable rechargeable battery that charges phones and other devices.

also_called: MagSafe power bank · Qi2 power bank
description: Power bank that attaches magnetically to the back of a phone and charges it wirelessly.
Pen made for the screen of one range of tablets or phones.
Cover with a keyboard made for one range of tablets.
Microphone made to plug into or clip onto a phone and record through it; one made for cameras that also takes a phone is in Cameras & Photography or Musical Instruments & Music Gear.
Weatherproof camera left outdoors and triggered by motion, mainly to film wildlife.
Cabinet or stand that combines a camera, light and printer to take pictures of guests.
Unmanned aircraft made for filming, carrying a stabilised camera.

also_called: viewfinder film camera · lo-fi film camera

description: Fabric box with a diffusion front that softens a light placed behind it; strip boxes and octaboxes are shapes of softbox.
Adjustable stand that carries a light or modifier; the C-stand is a heavier variant.
Stand and crossbar that hold a studio backdrop; the backdrop itself is in Soft Furnishings.
Darkroom projector that exposes a negative onto paper; condenser, diffusion and colour (dichroic) types.
Developer, stop bath, fixer and related chemistry for film and prints.
Light-sensitive paper for prints, including silver-gelatin (fibre or resin-coated), colour and inkjet photo paper.
Lensless spacer ring or tube fitted between body and lens so the lens focuses closer; bellows units are a variant.
Constant light with a tungsten-halogen lamp in an open-face or focusing housing; a tungsten Fresnel is listed under Fresnel light.
Daylight constant light with a metal-halide arc lamp run from a separate ballast; an HMI Fresnel is listed under Fresnel light.
Handgun with a revolving cylinder whose hammer is cocked by hand before each shot; percussion revolvers are listed here too.
Rifled long gun loaded with powder and bullet from the muzzle.
Smoothbore long gun loaded with powder and shot from the muzzle.

also_called: drilling · rifle-shotgun combination gun · Kombinierte Waffen

description: Air rifle that compresses its charge with a spring or gas piston at each cocking stroke.
Hand-held fork with elastic bands that launches a small projectile. A toy one is in Toys & Games.
Tube through which a dart is propelled by the breath. A toy one is in Toys & Games.
Single-edged, usually curved cavalry sword; national and regional patterns are sold under their own names.
Single-edged Japanese blade under one shaku (about 30 cm), counted as a sword by tradition.
Knife made for dressing and skinning game; skinning and caping knives are listed here too.
Hand-thrown star or spike with sharpened points. A toy one is in Toys & Games.
Shaft with a pointed head made for thrusting or throwing.
Compact CO2-powered launcher that fires self-defence projectiles; it may turn out to be the same product as the pepper-ball launcher.
Device that fires wired darts to deliver an incapacitating electric shock; Taser is the best-known brand.
Helmet made against bullets and fragments; sold by protection level.
Body armour made against knife and spike attacks (NIJ 0115.00 standard).
Vest made to hold hard armour plates; it counts as armour in its own right.
Complete suit of plate armour.
Black powder and its substitutes for muzzle-loading guns.
Shafted projectile shot from a bow.
Bullet sold on its own for loading cartridges.
Ignition cap sold on its own for loading cartridges.
Smokeless powder sold for loading cartridges.
Loose guard for a sword hilt.
Straight double-edged one-handed sword with a blade clearly shorter than an arming sword, often without a cross guard.
Broad single-edged one-handed European sword, straight or slightly curved, often widening towards the point.
Walking stick whose shaft hides a sword blade drawn from it. A cane without a blade is in Bags & Accessories or Health, Medical & Mobility.
Handgun with no magazine or cylinder, loaded by hand into one or two barrels (break-open, tip-up or falling block). Flintlock pistols are listed here too.
Shirt of interlinked metal rings worn as body armour; a mail coif goes with head armour.
Rigid plate defence of the torso, a breastplate alone or with its backplate, sold apart from a full harness.
Loose plate or mail armour for the neck and throat.
Loose collar and pommel cap made for a sword hilt, sold as a set; the Japanese pair is called fuchi-kashira.
Short-handled sickle blade made as a weapon, often used in pairs. A garden sickle is in Garden & Grounds.
Device fitted to a firearm muzzle that reduces the sound of a shot; its legal class varies by place.
Point fitted to an arrow or bolt shaft.
Centre section of a take-down bow, sold without limbs, that holds the grip, sight and rest.
Sealed carbon dioxide cartridge (8 g, 12 g, 88 g) that powers CO2 air guns and launchers.
Vinyl disc with fine grooves played at 33 1/3, 45 or another speed (LP, EP, single); diameter, speed, release type, weight and mastering are noted.
Shellac or early disc with wide grooves, played at about 78 rpm with a coarse stylus.
Audio tape in the standard two-hub compact cassette shell, pre-recorded or blank; the tape type is noted.
Audio tape in a cassette smaller than the compact cassette (microcassette, minicassette, picocassette).

also_called: compact disc · audio CD · HDCD · SHM-CD · Blu-spec CD2 · HQCD
description: 12 cm optical disc in the Compact Disc Digital Audio system (16-bit, 44.1 kHz), audiobook CDs included; HDCD and special pressings such as SHM-CD are noted.
Super Audio CD carrying DSD audio, single-layer or hybrid with a CD layer; whether it is hybrid is noted.
8 cm compact disc needing a tray recess or adapter.
Self-contained device sold with one work, usually an audiobook, fixed on it; it plays only that work.
12 cm optical disc in the Ultra HD Blu-ray system, sold apart from Blu-ray.
Book bound in rigid boards; binding (trade cloth, library or reinforced, leather or fine binding) and size are noted.

also_called: broché · poche · trade paperback · mass-market paperback
description: Book bound in a flexible paper cover, trade and mass-market alike; trim size and paper class are noted.
Book whose leaves are held by a wire or plastic spiral or comb.
Book issued as punched loose leaves held in a ring binder or post binding.
Short publication of a few sheets bound by staples or saddle-stitching.
Book printed on thick laminated paperboard pages, made for young children.
Book with pages of cloth, waterproof plastic or foam, made for babies.
Printed single-pattern sheet or envelope for sewing or knitting, issued loose rather than bound; craft, size range and garment are noted.
Comic issue of one serial number, stapled through the fold (the "floppy").
Softcover volume collecting several issues or chapters of a comic or manga.
Thick single volume collecting a long run of issues or several collected volumes; the binding is noted.
Periodical issued daily or weekly on unbound newsprint sheets; page format (broadsheet, Berliner, tabloid) is noted.
Periodical issue bound as a stapled or perfect-bound paper-covered booklet, digest-size magazines included; page format is noted.
Book-form volume binding together a run of issues of one periodical.
Printed map sheet folded to pocket size for carrying; the area covered is noted.
Book of maps bound in boards, a flexible cover or flexi-binding; the area covered is noted.
Publication issued as numbered parts sold weekly or monthly that together build one complete work; binders and models are sold apart.
One-off magazine-style publication with a book number, sold in bookshops and newsstands, often in a numbered series.
Commercially released film print on regular (double) 8 mm stock, needing a regular 8 projector.
Disc record cut with a vertical (hill-and-dale) groove, played with its own reproducer; Edison Diamond Disc and Pathé discs are examples.
16-inch disc made for broadcast playback on a transcription deck.
Cabinet, shelf or box shrine kept in a home or room to hold sacred images, name tablets or talismans. Comes in modern, karaki or gold-leaf styles, wall-hung or mini.
Rope hung to mark a sacred space or object in a rite. A seasonal festival decoration such as the kadomatsu is in Decor.
Sacred picture painted on a rigid panel, framed or mounted to stand or hang.
Large sacred picture or carved screen made to stand behind or above an altar, old-master altarpieces included.
Sculpted figure of a holy person, deity or saint made to be venerated.
Cross, with or without a figure on it, made to stand, hang or be held in veneration.
Boxed or composed set of figures and a stable showing the birth of Jesus, sold as one set.
Small model of a stupa or chorten made to stand on an altar as a sacred focus, filled with relics or mantras or not.
Body part or belonging of a holy person, or a thing touched to one, kept for veneration. Relics are classed first, second or third class.
String or loop of beads, knots or counters made to count prayers, with or without a cross, counter, tassel or guru bead. A necklace of the same beads made as jewellery is in Jewellery.
Rug or mat made to kneel, stand or prostrate on in prayer. Padding, non-slip base and surface fabric vary; a meditation cushion or mat is in Soft Furnishings.
Loose medal of a saint or sacred subject made for devotion. One made with a chain or bail to be worn is in Jewellery; one struck to commemorate or reward is in Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards.
Printed card with a sacred image or prayer, kept or carried for devotion.
Small charm carried, not worn as jewellery, for luck, protection or a named blessing. A worn one is in Jewellery; one issued for money is in Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards.
Cup or goblet made to hold wine or another drink used in a rite.
Plate or tray made to hold the symbolic foods of a rite. The food itself is not included.
Lidded cup, bowl or box made to hold consecrated or unconsecrated hosts.
Cup, usually two-handled, made to pour water over the hands in ritual washing.
Small box or tower made to hold fragrant spices smelled in the Havdalah rite.
Knife or blade made to be held in a rite, not to cut.
Spoon or ladle made to pour or offer water, ghee or a sacrament in a rite.
Case made to hold a doorpost scroll and be fixed to a doorpost. Comes in several materials.
Handwritten parchment strip of sacred text made to be put in a case and fixed to a doorpost. Script style and size (to fit the case) vary.
Handwritten scroll of the Five Books on parchment, made to be read in the rite. A printed Torah or Bible is in Media & Publications.
Bell held by a handle and rung in a rite or service.
Bowl-shaped bell that rests on a cushion or stand and is struck with a striker, made for a rite. A singing bowl made for music is in Musical Instruments & Music Gear.
Small two-headed hand drum, often hourglass-shaped with pellets on cords, rattled or struck in a rite. One sold for music is in Musical Instruments & Music Gear.
Pair of small thick cymbals joined by a cord, struck together in a rite. Ones sold for meditation are in Musical Instruments & Music Gear.
Lamp burning oil or ghee, made for worship.
Lamp kept burning before a sanctuary or altar. Electric or LED versions exist.
Candle holder made to stand on or by an altar in a rite. An open candle holder for the home is in Decor.

also_called: altar candle · votive candle · Easter candle · Yahrzeit candle
description: Candle made for a rite or devotion, including altar, votive, procession, Easter, grave, Yahrzeit and memorial candles.
Lantern made to be hung or set out in a rite or as a shrine offering. A garden stone lantern or decorative lantern is in Decor; a lantern made to be carried as a light is in Lighting.
Incense made for a rite, in stick, cone, resin or church grade. A smudge bundle made for a named rite is included.
Standing or hanging vessel for burning incense, including holders for the grave.
Incense burner hung on chains, to be swung.

also_called: rice vessel · tea cup · altar flower vase
description: Bowl, cup or vase made to hold water, rice, tea, flowers or other offerings, including flower vases for the grave.

also_called: church collection box · tzedakah box · saisen box

description: 78-card deck with major and minor suits, sold for divination. Each published deck design is listed under its publisher. A pack sold for card play is in Toys & Games.
Lettered board with a pointer, made for divination. One made as a board game is in Toys & Games.
Rod, pair of L-rods or forked rod made to be held for dowsing or divination. One sold as a survey or pipe-finding tool is in Tools & Workshop Equipment.
Box that holds a body for burial or cremation. Material, steel gauge, shape, sealing and biodegradable options vary; rental caskets are included.
Container for cremated remains, of any capacity from a keepsake portion to a companion pair. Not a worn piece of jewellery; pet urns are included.
Tablet that stands for a dead person, inscribed with a name, kept at an altar or home.
